articles.title: EU proposes giving Frontex border agency new major powers
articles.summary: The European Commission has unveiled a new plan to give Frontex more resources to ensure the return of irregular migrants, including by supporting non-EU countries. The move comes after the tragedy…

image.caption: The agency is set to be the central actor to ensure the return of irregular migrants [FILE: 2025]Image: NDR

blocks.text: The European Commission on Tuesdayunveiled a new proposal to beef up the powers of the EU border agency in order to empower it to support the return of irregular migrants.
The proposed legislation gives the agency, called Frontex, more resources to act beyond EU territory.
The plan would give the agency the power to support non-EU countries to return migrants to their countries of origin.
The proposal comes as EU member states increasingly focus on returns, saying too many people who are asked to leave the bloc remain.
EU border agency to be beefed up after Ceuta humanitarian crisis of summer
The new role for Frontex comes after the humanitarian crisis in Ceuta this summer.
The tragedy in the Spanish exclave was seized upon by some EU member states as an example of where the EU could do more to block people from reaching the EU.
Italy, for example, placed some temporary border controls on travel from Spain.
Spain's prime minister at the time criticized several EU member states for their "selfish" response to the influx of migrants to Ceuta.
"Today we propose that Frontex becomes the central EU actor on returns," Magnus Brunner, commissioner for internal affairs ​and migration, told reporters.
"It will be able to act faster, with a quick reaction force that can ⁠deploy within ⁠24 hours and spot risks ⁠early, before an ​event becomes a crisis," Brunner added.
How the far right hardened Europe's migration stance
Frontex to be given wide powers to support deportation of irregular migrants

The ability to deport migrants from non-EU countries means that Frontex could, for instance, deport a Bangladeshi national from Libya, where many migrants start the final leg of their journey into the bloc.
The plan envisages gradually expanding Frontex's standing corps to 30,000 officers by creating a new "European border and return reserve" of 17,000 officers within the next 15 years.
Those officers would remain at the disposal of member states and could be deployed when needed, the commission said in a statement.
The proposal would also create a new EU Return Coordination Center within Frontex and expand the agency's role across the entire deportation process.
It would also include a new online monitoring center to track border-related developments on social media and support action against content linked to border security risks.
Frontex reform criticized by rights groups
Frontex has been responsible for guarding the external borders of the EU as well as ensuring the rights of new arrivals.
It has been criticized for its lack of accountability in the past.
The planned reform shrinks the scope of the agency's internal rights watchdog, with complaints to be referred to national authorities.
"The Commission is pandering to populism and the far right on migration," said Tineke Strik, a Dutch MEP from the Greens/EFA group.
"We need a human rights-based approach to border management and Frontex plays a key role. But instead the Commission ​risks turning Frontex into a European version of ICE," she said.
Edited: Alex Berry

articles.title: Noah Wyle named People's Sexiest Man Alive
articles.summary: Noah Wyle, the 55-year-old star of HBO's smash-hit The Pitt, has been crowned People magazine's Sexiest Man Alive for 2026, a designation that some fans are cheering, while others are asking for a…

image.caption: Noah Wyle arrives at the annual Fashion Los Angeles Awards on April 14, in Beverly Hills, Calif. (Jordan Strauss/Invision/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Noah Wyle, the 55-year-old star of HBO's smash-hit The Pitt, has been crowned People magazine's Sexiest Man Alive for 2026, a designation that some fans are cheering, while others are asking for a second opinion.
The magazine announced Tuesday that Wyle was just what the doctor ordered for this year
Move over McDreamy — there's a new TV doctor running up heartbeats in hospital scrubs, at least according to People magazine.
Noah Wyle, the 55-year-old star of HBO's smash-hit The Pitt, has been crowned People's latest Sexiest Man Alive.
When he first got the news, he thought it "sounded like a prank," Wyle said in the People interview released Tuesday. But his wife was able to convince him it was probably real.
"She was very pleased that this reflects well on her taste," he joked, adding that he expected to "take a lot of ribbing from friends and family," once the news came out.

#NoahWyle is PEOPLE’s 2026 #SexiestManAlive! Watch our video interview in the #PeopleApp, and read the full issue two days early as a #PeopleVIP. https://t.co/QeP1StmEJb 📷️: Jeff Lipsky https://t.co/PsRXGZWrea—people

Wyle first charmed audiences with a stethoscope in the 90s as Dr. John Carter in NBC's medical drama ER. The show was a massive hit, garnering attention for both its heavy-hitting plotlines and its swoony-worthy cast; Wyle was one of several ER cast members who graced the cover of a 1996 "Sexy Men of ER" issue of People magazine, and his ER costar George Clooney was given the Sexiest Man Alive designation twice.

Wyle went on to star in The Librarian film franchise in the 2000s and garnered praise for appearances in series like The Red Line (2019) and Leverage: Redemption (2021-2025), but it was his return to the medical world in 2025 as Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch in The Pitt that launched him back into the headlines.
Wyle and George Clooney, left, the stars of ER, arrive for the 48th Annual Emmy Awards in Pasadena, Calif., in 1996. (Vince Bucci/AFP/Getty Images)

The show quickly became a cultural phenomenon, averaging more than 18 million viewers per episode after the full first season dropped, according to parent company Warner Bros. Discovery, and racking up 13 prime-time Emmy nominations in its first year and 25 in its second.
Wyle has won the Emmy for outstanding lead actor in a drama series two years in a row for his work on the show.
He told People that, sexiest man title or not, he still feels most comfortable when acting.
Wyle poses for photographers at the HBO Max Experience in London in March. (Carlo Paloni/Invision/The Associated Press)

articles.title: Schrödinger’s racism, Nige’s latest wheeze to dodge his associates’ bigotry | John Crace
articles.summary:
We are apparently to believe Raheem Kassam calling Kemi a ‘Nigerian scammer’ was racist and not racist at the same time

Back to the future. Some of us can remember the days when the key to…

blocks.text: Back to the future. Some of us can remember the days when the key to surviving a nuclear war was to kneel down under the kitchen table and keep your eyes closed till you were incinerated or died of radiation poisoning. Now the government wants you to hoard some baked beans and a few litres of water in the hope of getting through the next three days.

But when the apocalypse does come, you can bank on there being one survivor. The politician with seemingly limitless powers of regeneration. As one party of his dies, so another rises from the ashes. Fuelled not by water and tinned food, but by alcohol and grievance. Somehow, Nigel Farage is always the victim in his own story. The man who is forever misunderstood.

Nige must be the unluckiest politician alive. The man who has only ever wanted the best for everybody – deporting immigrants is clearly in their own best interests, even if it involves death or torture – keeps getting mired in scandal. There’s the money. Of course there is. Plenty of it from – how shall we put this? – unorthodox sources. But there’s also the racism. Why is it that so many who are close to Farage and his organisation turn out to be bigots? How can his message of love and peace to all men be so tainted? It’s happened so often now that you could forgive Nige for being a little grumpy.

Last week one of his closest friends was at it again. Raheem Kassam, touted as Reform’s next chief of staff, called Kemi Badenoch a “Nigerian scammer”. You and I know exactly what he meant. The leader of the opposition was like a West African phonejacker who rang you up and tried to scam your bank accounts. It was a fairly obvious racist slur. One designed to denigrate.

blocks.caption: Nige chats to his ‘not friend’ Raheem Kassam at a New York Gala in 2024. Photograph: Laura Brett/Zuma Press Wire/REX/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Only it wasn’t quite so obviously racist to Reform MPs themselves. Robert Jenrick called it a bit of forensic journalism. At least that’s what he implied by describing Kassam as a journalist. Danny Kruger was even more confused. There again, he often is. He’s meant to be the intellectual and moral compass of Reform, but just appears dim-witted and spinning helplessly in space. He thought “Nigerian scammer” couldn’t be racist because he couldn’t conceive of any of Nigel’s friends being racist. Try a little harder, Danny.

It was third time unlucky – that word again – as Nige took on his first proper morning media round in months. It didn’t end well for him. Car-crash TV. On BBC Breakfast, the presenter Sally Nugent quickly cut to the chase and it soon became clear that Nige doesn’t take it well when an intelligent woman asks him tricky questions. He likes to think of himself very much as a man’s man. Somehow being interviewed by a woman is a sign of disrespect. Or maybe he’s still tetchy about having given a press conference to a near-empty hall the day before.

First Nige tried to claim Kassam had not been a former chief of staff – he had in one of Farage’s previous lives – and was on the point of saying he wasn’t even a friend. But then he had a brainwave. “He’s Indian,” he said. “He’s of Indian heritage.” As if that somehow precluded all Indians – all black and brown people, for that matter – from being racist. A suggestion, dare one say it, that is racist in itself. Nige clearly believes in a hierarchy of racism. If he believes in racism at all. Maybe we’re just all stuck in a doom loop of cultural relativism. We just need to chill out a bit.
after newsletter promotion

Next Farage tried to play the word dissociation game. Just because Kassam had used the words “Nigerian scammer” in conjunction with one another, it didn’t necessarily mean the words were in any way connected to form a single image. All he had done was to state two truths. Kemi was of Nigerian descent, though for the purposes of this conversation he was prepared to concede that she might also be part British. And she was a scammer, because she had said things that were demonstrably untrue. Much the same could be said of Nige, mind. Maybe in his own mind he also longs to be outed as a scammer.

Back in the BBC studio, Nugent wasn’t having any of this and kept at him. Did he think it was racist? “No, I don’t,” said Nige. Perhaps a bit over the top, but definitely not intentionally racist. Farage had spoken, Schrödinger’s racism. Something could be racist and not racist at the same time. In any case, he couldn’t be held responsible for any of the social media posts his friends and supporters made. It was his curse that so many in Reform expressed themselves in racist language. He had no idea why he had become the last refuge for so many bigots.

Things took on a more surreal turn later that morning when Kassam emailed a Guardian journalist to give an update on the situation. In it, he said that Nige had given him a ticking off for a tweet that was neither “clever nor funny”. Just a shame Farage couldn’t have used his position as the leader of Reform to make that same point on the BBC hours earlier. Kassam went on to say that, in hindsight, his tweet could have been better phrased and timed. He also claimed Kemi was a con artist for turning the Tories into a version of the Lib Dems. That will come as news to both the Tories and the Lib Dems. The Tories have been shadowing Reform to the right for the last two years.

The real sorry-not-sorry moment came when Kassam suggested he had spent too much time in the US recently. Over there, out-and-out racism was an acceptable rite of political discourse. People could say what they want. The trouble is that we Brits had lost our sense of humour. It was now a thought crime even to make a racist joke. Time we all lightened up. What was needed was more politicians who called Kemi a “Nigerian scammer” not fewer.

This isn’t quite the end of it. Because Kassam’s new found contrition may not be all it seems. On Tuesday morning he was again posting about “Kemi Scammenoch” on X. A post that has been subsequently deleted. As has his pinned “Nigerian scammer” tweet. If this is remorse, it’s still in its early days. Maybe one should treat Kassam and Farage as one and the same. When they show you what they are, believe them.

articles.title: Homes across UK to get low- or no-interest loans to fund solar panels and heat pumps
articles.summary:
Government-backed Warm Home Loans scheme to help households cut energy bills by hundreds of pounds

Households across the UK can now cut their energy bills by hundreds of pounds a year at no…

blocks.text: Households across the UK can now cut their energy bills by hundreds of pounds a year at no upfront cost by applying for interest-free or “low-interest” loans to fund upgrades such as heat pumps, batteries and solar panels.

The government-backed Warm Home Loans scheme, which launched on Tuesday, could mean thousands more households are able to access low-carbon energy alternative technologies, thanks to loans ranging from £7,500 to up £35,000.

Energy suppliers including British Gas and E.On have partnered with lenders from Tandem Bank and Homeserve respectively to offer the loans directly to customers at a discounted rate compared with those offered by high street lenders.

People interested in swapping their gas boiler for an air-source or ground-source heat pump could secure loans of up to £10,000 or £35,000 respectively, while also drawing on the government’s existing scheme which offers grants of up to £9,000 a year for households installing the replacements for fossil fuel heating.
Installing a heat pump, battery and solar panels could save households up to £550 a year on their energy bills, rising by a further £300 a year with a time-of-use tariff, according to the government.

Soaring energy costs have led to record demand for low-carbon home energy upgrades over the last year, and the government believes the loan scheme means “thousands more households” will be able to cut their energy bills by fitting clean energy technology and spreading repayments over many years.

Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, said: “Energy is an everyday essential that must be affordable for everyone. These government-supported loans will help families across the UK upgrade their homes with no upfront costs to make them warmer and cheaper to run.”

Chris Norbury, the chief executive of E.On UK, said that a recent trial showed that fuel-poor customers in Coventry were able to save more than £250 a year on average by combining a home battery with a time of use tariff that charges lower rates for using energy outside peak demand hours.
He said the Warm Homes Loan scheme was “an opportunity to take that further” by “removing barriers to low-carbon technologies”.

The government set out the terms of the new scheme a day before the chancellor, John Healey, delivers his first budget on Wednesday, which reportedly will include plans to scale back heat pump grants made through its boiler upgrade scheme.

The scheme is not expected to be scrapped altogether, but sources say hundreds of millions of pounds will be cut from its £2.7bn five-year budget because Treasury officials consider it a subsidy used mainly by middle-class households.
It has typically provided grants of up to £7,500 to help meet the £13,600 cost of installing a heat pump, meaning households have still required a significant outlay to make up the difference.

The Guardian understands that grants of up to £9,000 a year are likely to remain available to households that are not connected to the gas grid and are forced to rely on high-cost heating oil. These grants could be used alongside the low-interest loans to cover the full cost of a heat pump.
Other lenders taking part in the Warm Home Loans scheme include HTG Finance, Propensio, Secure Trust Bank, Selina Finance, South Manchester Credit Union, Sunsave, The Money Co-op and This Bank.

articles.title: Slovenia mourns loss of glacier on its highest peak after scorching summer
articles.summary:
Extreme heat accelerated disappearance of Triglav glacier from mountain revered as a symbol of Slovenian identity

The final ice patch has vanished from Slovenia’s Triglav glacier, the…

blocks.text: The final ice patch has vanished from Slovenia’s Triglav glacier, the latest Alpine casualty of Europe’s scorching summer.

The once mighty ice mass lost 93% of its surface area between 1983 and 2003, shrinking to cover less than a hectare of overheated rock, but went on to surprise researchers who feared its imminent demise, clinging on to the mountain for two more decades.

In the last five years, which includes Europe’s three hottest years on record, the remaining ice has melted to a handful of isolated pockets, with the final remnant of the main body measuring just a few metres by the end of summer. New photos of the mountainside – taken either side of snowfall this month – confirm that no ice remains.

blocks.caption: The last piece of the Triglav glacier, pictured on 2 October. Photograph: Borut Živulovič/Reuters

blocks.text: Matija Zorn, director of the Anton Melik Geographical Institute, said Mount Triglav “holds a central place in Slovenian national identity” and the demise of the glacier represents the loss of an important data source and indicator of climate change.
“Every year I knew that the ice was going to be less and less,” he said. “But I was shocked every year [by] how much less ice was up there.”

Fierce heatwaves made hotter by carbon pollution have ravaged the Alps and reduced big white glaciers to what scientists have called “moonlike” rock deserts. Last month, Swiss glaciologists found that nearly a fifth of the country’s ice had disappeared in the last five years, with a 5.5% drop in volume in 2026.

In Slovenia, home to the south-eastern tip of the Alps, the Triglav glacier suffered most of its decline in the last century. Historical photographs and documents suggest the glacier covered about 40 hectares in the mid-1800s. By 1946, when scientists conducted the first formal measurements, its area had shrunk to just 14 hectares.

Zorn, who first took measurements at the glacier in 2001, said the rate of change was surprising even in the decades in which the glacier defied expectations. The spot at which he had to put on crampons to prevent slipping jumped back year after year as the glacier receded.

“The melting is incredible,” he said. “In 2002 … we took a core of ice out for some geochemical analysis and it was like 5 metres [deep]. The next year, I was standing on the same spot … not on ice, but on rock.”
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Triglav appears on Slovenia’s flag. Illustration: Wikimedia

blocks.text: Triglav is Slovenia’s highest peak, a cultural touchpoint that every person in the country of skiers and climbers is expected to climb at least once. Although the glacier has vanished, scientists have found ice in the caves beneath Triglav as its retreat has exposed new shafts. A second glacier on the Skuta mountain has also shrunk and thinned, but the remaining patch of ice is better shaded than Triglav and is expected to hold out for a few more years.

blocks.caption: Glaciers in the French Alps are also melting fast as a result of climate change. Photograph: Jeff Pachoud/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Western Europe suffered through its hottest summer on record this year, causing at least 50,000 estimated heat deaths and costly secondary effects that ranged from failed harvests to power plants being forced to shut down. Scientists are still assessing the damage done to ecosystems.
Miha Pavšek, a glaciologist and mountain guide, said “nature is changing in front of our eyes” but people were not yet taking it seriously.

“With the melting of the glacier, a part of me is also going away,” said Pavšek, who has a photograph of his parents there in 1957. “There are some things that humans thought were eternal. Glaciers are obviously not.”

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro's passports cancelled after he fails to surrender them
articles.summary: The defeated presidential candidate is under investigation for alleged money laundering and barred from leaving Brazil.

blocks.text: Police in Brazil say they have cancelled the passports of the defeated right-wing presidential candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, after he failed to comply with an order to surrender the documents.
On Monday, the Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro to hand his passports over to police within 24 hours as part of an investigation into alleged money laundering, which he denies.
At the time, Bolsonaro said he had no plans to leave the country, and insisted that he would stay in Brazil to lead the opposition to his left-wing rival, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
However, the deadline has passed without the senator surrendering the passports, prompting speculation he may have left the country.
Federal officers are checking border crossings to establish if Bolsonaro may have travelled to neighbouring Argentina, according to a police source consulted by BBC News Brasil.
However, Argentine authorities have told the BBC there is no record of Bolsonaro entering their country through any border crossing.

Bolsonaro was already under investigation for alleged corruption over the financing of a film about his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who was convicted of plotting a coup and is under house arrest.
In addition to that investigation, Brazil's Supreme Court ordered police on Tuesday to probe Flávio Bolsonaro's electoral campaign over alleged foreign funding.
The 45-year-old senator suffered a stinging defeat on Sunday when he was beaten by Lula in a presidential run-off, which Bolsonaro had been widely expected to win.
Opinion polls had put him narrowly ahead of Lula and analysts pointed out that Bolsonaro's win in the first round of the election on 4 October, meant he was likely to take victory in the run-off.
But after an early lead in the count, he was overtaken by the veteran incumbent, who became the first presidential candidate to overturn a first round loss to win in the second round.
Lula won 51.79% of the vote, compared to Bolsonaro's 48.21%.
Despite trailing by 4.4 million votes, Bolsonaro has not conceded and has called for the election to be annulled.
He argues that he was put at a disadvantage because polling was extended by two hours on election day - even though the extension was requested by both his party and that of his rival.
He called the extension, which was ordered by a Supreme Court justice, a "dirty trick".
However the party he represented, the Liberal Party, has accepted the result, although it did say that the extension of voting "merits investigation".

articles.title: Canada's new relationship with EU will be 'closer to membership' than ever, senior officials say

image.caption: Prime Minister Mark Carney is seen at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France, last month — where the idea of associate EU membership for Canada was formally announced. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New

European Union officials say the details and exact title of Canada's possible associate EU membership are still being internally debated — but the 27 countries are united in wanting the "closest possible association" with Canada.
Associate membership expected to be main topic at summit this week in Montreal
· CBC News
· Posted: Oct 27, 2026 12:46 PM EDT | Last Updated: 14 minutes ago

Canada will host the EU at a summit in Montreal this week where the two sides are expected to announce new agreements on a number of key areas of co-operation, including trade, security and technology.

This year's meeting will be one of the "most important summits the European Union has ever held," one senior EU official said, speaking on background during a press briefing Tuesday morning in Brussels.
"It's building a partnership that comes closer to membership than anything we've ever done before."
Is Canada becoming an ‘associate member’ of the European Union?
However, the process is just getting started, officials stressed.
"This is uncharted territory. This is also the work that will need to be done between now and the next summit," they said, which is expected to be held in 2027.
The officials acknowledged some member states have questions about what Canada's new role will actually mean.
"There is no questioning from the member state side on their ambition for this relationship," an official said.
Carney says summit launches year of talks

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen surprised many last month when she announced the EU would begin the process of making Canada its first "associate member," a status that does not exist within the bloc.

Prime Minister Mark Carney responded the next day during a speech to the European Parliament that Canada welcomed "the ambition" of associate membership, later telling reporters it was the substance of the relationship that mattered more than the name itself.

Speaking on Tuesday in Ottawa on his way into a cabinet meeting, Carney reiterated that stance, saying the two-day summit that begins Thursday would be the launch of formal discussions and negotiations over the next year.
EU agreement 'names or nomenclature' don't matter, says Carney
"The good news is it doesn't matter about specific names or nomenclature," Carney said.
"What matters is the difference that it will make to the lives of Canadians … and Canada as a whole becoming a more independent, more sovereign nation, so we can live our lives as we choose."
Associate membership would be unique to Canada
There are many unanswered questions about what associate membership would require from Canada and what it would mean for the other European countries that have spent years trying to join the EU.
Officials said Tuesday this type of associate membership would be specific to Canada.
"We're embarking on the start of a journey, so let's not already now determine exactly how far we go," they said.

items: Far right gains ground in Europe as Canada pivots from Trump to EU
PQ accuses Ottawa of muzzling Quebec during upcoming Canada-EU summit

blocks.text: Officials would not say whether other countries had approached the EU looking to form a similar relationship as Canada's.
Carney has repeatedly stated that Canada is not seeking full EU membership, and often refers to the enhanced partnership as a "strategic alliance."

The prime minister has been aggressively seeking out stronger diplomatic and trade ties with other countries, including in Europe, as relations between the U.S. and Canada continue to suffer under the trade war, with U.S. President Donald Trump's escalating tariffs and ongoing threats to annex Canada.

Marina von Stackelberg is a senior reporter at CBC's Parliamentary Bureau in Ottawa. She recently worked in Berlin as a recipient of the 2026 Arthur F. Burns fellowship. She covers national politics with a focus on health, labour, and the NDP. Marina previously worked as a reporter and host in Winnipeg, with earlier stints in Halifax and Sudbury. Connect with her by email at mvs@cbc.ca or on social media @CBCMarina.

articles.title: Doctor performs first telerobotic surgery in US, removing prostate from 35 miles away
articles.summary:
The patient was at a facility in Minneola, Florida, while the surgeon operated remotely from another facility

A Florida surgeon has…

blocks.text: A Florida surgeon has performed the first telerobotic operation between two US hospitals, removing the prostate of a man with cancer from 35 miles away, according to officials.

Dr Vipul Patel, founder and medical director of the Global Robotics Institute at AdventHealth Celebration in suburban Orlando, on Sunday performed an investigational robotic prostatectomy on a 66-year-old prostate cancer patient who volunteered for a clinical study evaluating a robotic telesurgery system.

The patient, identified as Mark, was at an AdventHealth facility in Minneola, Florida, while Patel operated remotely from another AdventHealth facility in the community of Celebration. Study co-principal investigator and surgeon Marcio Moschovas provided onsite support to Mark during the procedure, an AdventHealth news release said.
Mark was recovering well after the procedure, AdventHealth told ABC.

The surgery was part of a clinical research study conducted under a Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved investigational device exemption. Such an authorization permits the system to be studied but does not constitute FDA approval or clearance.

The procedure done on Mark came after 10 investigational telesurgeries between Orlando, Florida, and Luanda, Angola, while marking the study’s expansion into US hospitals, AdventHealth’s news release said.

“For generations, access to highly specialized care has often depended on where a patient lives,” a statement attributed to Patel said. His statement added: “This study allows us to evaluate whether telesurgery could one day help reduce geographic barriers to specialized treatment.”

Telesurgery allows surgeons to control robotic instruments remotely but researchers are still evaluating its safety, reliability and cybersecurity. AdventHealth said no previous reports had documented a telesurgery procedure between two US locations and cautioned that Sunday’s surgery did not establish the technology’s general clinical performance.

Robotic prostatectomy carries risks including bleeding, infection, incontinence and erectile dysfunction – as well as the possibility of switching to open surgery. Telesurgery adds risks such as equipment or connection failures and cybersecurity threats, making it essential for there to be an on-site team to take over if needed.

Sunday’s procedure in Florida unfolded after a similar headline-making operation just months earlier, when a surgeon in London used a four-armed robot equipped with a 3D camera to remove a man’s prostate in Gibraltar, about 1,500 miles away.
The London-Gibraltar surgery was successful, with a lag of just 0.06 seconds between the surgeon’s movements and the robot’s response.

articles.title: Mbappe apologizes as Chinese sponsors drop him and TV broadcasts are halted over Mao dictator remark
articles.summary: French soccer star Kylian Mbappe has apologized after apparently referring to Mao Zedong as a dictator. Chinese sponsors have dropped him, while state television has suspended Spanish league…

image.caption: Mbappe's comments sparked a backlash in China, costing him sponsorship deals [FILE: 18/07/2026]Image: Paul Childs/REUTERS

blocks.text: France striker Kylian Mbappe apologized after apparently referring to China's founding leader Mao Zedong as a dictator in a video that circulated online.
The controversy prompted three major Chinese companies to sever sponsorship ties with the Real Madrid forward, while Chinese state television suspended broadcasts of Spain's La Liga.
What did Mbappe say about Mao?
The controversy began when a video circulated showing Mbappe discussing his favorite internet meme featuring himself.

In the clip, apparently filmed ahead of an appearance on the French online talk show The Bridge, Mbappe referred to an image depicting his face superimposed on the body of "some guy ... I think he's a Chinese dictator."

The image appeared to depict Mao Zedong, who founded the People's Republic of China in 1949 and ruled until his death in 1976. Jokes about country’s former leader and descriptions of him as a dictator remain taboo.
Mbappe has previously been depicted as authoritarian leaders in online memes mocking his perceived influence over teammates the suggestions that he has the power to influence club decisions.
Mbappe has been nicknamed "the dictator" in the European press.
How did Mbappe apologize?
"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," Mbappe said in a statement.
"I apologize to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry."

blocks.caption: Mao remains revered by many in China despite his policies causing tens of millions of deaths (FILE: 01/10/1949)Image: AP

blocks.text: Chinese sponsors cut ties with Mbappe
Chinese beverage company Dongpeng, dairy producer Mengniu and cheesemaker Milkground announced they were ending their partnerships with the French international.
In similarly worded statements, each said that they oppose "any words and actions that hurt national sentiment."
China Media Group, which oversees state broadcaster CCTV, also suspended broadcasts of La Liga matches and removed advertisements featuring Mbappe.
La Liga apologized for the controversy, saying Mbappe's comments were made in a personal capacity and did not represent the Spanish league.
Chinese state broadcaster CCTV subsequently said it would consider Mbappe's apology but would also judge his future actions.

In response to a question about the controversy, China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said that "words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."
Why is Mao such a sensitive subject in China?
Mao remains a revered figure in China, where public criticism of the former Communist leader is politically sensitive.
His rule was also marked by disastrous political campaigns, including the Great Leap Forward, which contributed to a famine that killed tens of millions of people.
The ruling Communist Party acknowledges some of his mistakes but maintains that his achievements outweighed them, making criticism of his legacy politically sensitive.

articles.title: Federal agents search Beverly Hills mansion tied to ex-congressman Eric Swalwell
articles.summary:
Home of wealthy developer Stephen Cloobeck searched in connection to sexual misconduct inquiry into Swalwell

Federal law enforcement agents searched a home in suburban

blocks.text: Federal law enforcement agents searched a home in suburban Los Angeles early on Tuesday as part of an investigation into Eric Swalwell, who resigned from Congress amid a wave of sexual misconduct allegations, a law enforcement official and two people familiar with the investigation told the Associated Press.

Agents searched the Beverly Hills home of the wealthy developer and Swalwell donor Stephen Cloobeck, where the Democratic ex-congressman spent time before resigning from office in April, according to the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss the investigation.
Swalwell has denied criminal wrongdoing.
Messages seeking comment were left for Swalwell’s attorney and for a lawyer who represented Cloobeck in another matter.
Cloobeck, the founder of the Diamond Resorts International timeshare company, told the New York Post in April that he cut ties with Swalwell as accusations against him mounted.
“I am no longer associated with a man that takes advantage of women,” Cloobeck told the newspaper. “I support women’s rights.”

Tuesday’s search is the latest escalation in the federal investigation of Swalwell – one of several investigations begun after a woman came forward with allegations that he sexually assaulted her twice, including when she worked for him.

The San Francisco Chronicle, followed by CNN, first reported the allegations. CNN also reported that three other women alleged various kinds of sexual misconduct by Swalwell, including sending them unsolicited explicit messages or nude photos.

Asked about the search at Cloobeck’s address, an FBI spokesperson, Lourdes Arocho, said the bureau “early this morning … conducted an operation in the Los Angeles region related to an ongoing criminal investigation.
“We have no further comment.”
In August, federal agents seized electronic devices from Swalwell at the San Francisco airport and searched his Washington DC home.

Swalwell, an Iowa native, was elected in 2012 and represented a House district east of San Francisco. He launched a presidential run in April 2019 but ended it a few months later after failing to catch on with voters.
The seven-term lawmaker had been seen as one of the leading candidates in California’s gubernatorial race before dropping out after the allegations surfaced.
after newsletter promotion

The office of the Manhattan district attorney, Alvin Bragg, has said it is also investigating Swalwell after a former staffer told CNN and the Chronicle that Swalwell raped her at a hotel while he was in New York City for a charity gala in 2024.
In a statement, Bragg’s office encouraged “survivors and anyone with knowledge of these allegations to contact” its special victims division.
Los Angeles prosecutors were also said to be weighing charges.

Swalwell was one of Donald Trump’s top antagonists in Congress. He was a prominent member of the House judiciary and intelligence committees during Trump’s first presidency and served as one of several Democratic prosecutors for Trump’s second impeachment after the 6 January 2021 attack on the US Capitol.

Swalwell was removed from the intelligence committee by the then US House speaker, Kevin McCarthy, a California Republican, in 2023 based on Swalwell’s contact with a suspected Chinese spy, Christine Fang.
Fang was reported to have come into contact with Swalwell’s campaign as he was first running for Congress in 2012 and to have participated in fundraising for his 2014 campaign.

Federal investigators alerted Swalwell to their concerns and briefed Congress about Fang in 2015, at which point Swalwell says he cut off contact with her. He was not accused of wrongdoing, and a House ethics committee investigation that was opened in 2021 closed two years later without any action.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro rumoured to have fled Brazil after presidential election loss
articles.summary:
Authorities demanded he hand over his passport after loss to Lula but far-right senator remains unaccounted for

The far-right senator

blocks.text: The far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro has not been seen since Monday and missed a Tuesday-morning deadline to hand his passport to the federal police, fuelling rumours that he may have fled Brazil after losing Sunday’s presidential election.

A supreme court justice cancelled Bolsonaro’s passport minutes after the result in a ruling related to a criminal case against the senator. He had until 11am to surrender the document to the federal police, but did not appear.

The Argentinian news website Infobae reported that on Monday night he reportedly fled to Argentina, where he was expected to board a private jet in Puerto Iguazú bound for the US, but the plane did not take off.

Bolsonaro, who has yet to concede defeat to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, posted a video on Monday in which, commenting on the cancellation of his passport, he said: “I never thought about leaving the country.”
One of the senator’s brothers, the former congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro, who is in self-imposed exile in the US, had said in an interview last Friday that his brother should leave Brazil if he lost.
The Brazilian newspaper Folha de S Paulo reported that allies in the Bolsonaro family’s inner circle had been told that he had indeed left for Argentina and intended to travel from there to the US.

As there is no record of him passing through any regular Brazilian immigration checkpoint, the federal police are trying to establish from Argentinian authorities whether there is any record of him entering the country.
The Argentinian channel Todo Noticias reported that the senator had reportedly crossed the border into Argentina on foot and abandoned plans to board the plane once news of his movements leaked.

Bolsonaro was told to surrender his passport over a criminal case in which the federal police are investigating him for possible involvement in a money-laundering scheme worth about £680m ($905m) involving betting companies.

The senator’s possible flight makes the future of the far right after the presidential election even more uncertain. The family patriarch, Jair Bolsonaro, is under house arrest for attempting a coup, and one of his sons is in the US and the whereabouts of another unclear.

Eduardo Bolsonaro has an outstanding arrest warrant against him in Brazil, after being sentenced to four years in prison for trying to interfere in his father’s trial by lobbying Donald Trump to impose sanctions on the justices hearing the case.
Political scientist Magna Inácio, a professor at the Federal University of Minas Gerais, believes a power vacuum may now emerge within the right.
“The resistance of Brazilian voters to handing victory to this more extremist camp sends a signal that the right leadership is now up for grabs,” she said.

Since Jair Bolsonaro, then a career congressman with few laws to his name, surprisingly won the presidency in 2018, there has effectively been no right wing in Brazil, only the far-right Bolsonarismo movement.
after newsletter promotion

Camila Rocha, a political scientist who studies Brazil’s new right, believes the fact that three Bolsonaros are now potentially out of the picture could trigger a “shift in power” away from blood ties.

“I think there is a tendency for power to move away from the sons,” said Rocha, noting that before the election, polls showed Jair Bolsonaro supporters preferred other potential candidates over his eldest son, including Jair Bolsonaro’s wife, Michelle Bolsonaro, who was recently elected senator, and the São Paulo governor, Tarcísio de Freitas.

Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly did not want to run because he thought a presidential campaign would turn his life into “hell”, and believed his re-election to the senate was assured. But with Eduardo, his father’s “plan A”, now living in the US, the senator was chosen to run.

Most observers agree that Flávio lacks his father’s charisma. He had a 24-year political career in which he passed very few laws as a state legislator and senator, and the only previous time he ran for executive office was for mayor of Rio de Janeiro in 2016, when he fainted during a televised debate and finished fourth.

Even in a family frequently embroiled in legal trouble he stood out, facing longstanding criminal allegations, including suspicions that he embezzled part of his staff’s salaries, as well as more recent accusations.
Even so, 48.21% of Brazilians voted for Flávio Bolsonaro on Sunday, which many analysts see as both an anti-Lula vote and a vote for whomever Jair Bolsonaro had chosen.

Inácio believes the struggle over the Bolsonaro legacy will also play out among family members who remain in Brazil, including Michelle and Bolsonaro’s other political sons, the senator-elect Carlos Bolsonaro and congressman-elect Jair Renan Bolsonaro, who publicly do not get along with their stepmother.

“Michelle clearly has a political project of her own, but she is likely to face strong resistance from the two stepsons who are in congress. It is only a matter of time before tensions between them grow,” said the political scientist.

articles.title: ICC prosecution seeks admission of testimonies on Bato, drug war target lists
articles.summary: PRAGUE, Czech Republic - International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors are asking Trial Chamber III to admit yet another batch of recorded testimonies--this time, of two witnesses who allegedly…
articles.byline: ANDY PEÑAFUERTE III, JAY-VEE MARASIGAN PANGAN

blocks.text: PRAGUE, Czech Republic – International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors are asking Trial Chamber III to admit yet another batch of recorded testimonies—this time, of two witnesses who allegedly provided evidence on Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa’s role in the Duterte administration’s drug war.

In a public redacted filing dated October 26, Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang sought to admit the previously recorded statements of witnesses P-1334 and P-1348 in place of their live testimony, citing ICC Rules of Procedure and Evidence rule 68(2)(b).

Niang stated that the two witnesses also provided evidence on roles in the implementation of former President Rodrigo Duterte’s war on drugs and a shift in the conduct of certain actors after he became president, although several details remain redacted.
Their statements mention “target lists of drug personalities”, and alleged “killing quotas and financial rewards," the prosecution said.
P-1334 statement on Bato’s role in Duterte’s drug war

Witness P-1334—who is referred to in the filing using female pronouns—described the establishment, structure, reporting lines, and key personnel of a redacted entity, as well as Dela Rosa’s alleged role during Duterte’s anti-drug campaign.
Dela Rosa was chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP) from July 2016 to April 2018.

The prosecution said P-1334 addressed Dela Rosa’s “proximity [REDACTED] leadership," to which she described him as being “in charge of disseminating his instructions to terminate people during Mr. Duterte’s anti-drug campaign.”
The public filing does not identify whose instructions were being referred to.
P-1334 also allegedly provided evidence on efforts to identify and prioritize individuals for inclusion in target lists of suspected drug personalities and on killings linked to the alleged policy.
“The evidence of P-1334 also relates to Incidents 13 and 53,” Niang stated.

In the trial brief, the prosecution referred to Incident 13 as the shootout that killed Rolando Espinosa Sr., the former mayor of Albuera, Leyte, and Raul Yap, both of whom were suspected of being involved in the illicit drug trade.

Incident 53 detailed the killing of an alleged drug pusher and another victim, who were shot by PNP Anti-Illegal Drugs Group (AIDG) operatives. The trial brief noted that the police report on this incident “falsely stated” that the victims were killed in self-defense.
P-1348 statement on ‘target list’

Meanwhile, Witness P-1348—mentioned in the document using male pronouns—allegedly described anti-drug operations before July 2016, the killing of some individuals appearing on redacted lists, and an increase in killings after Duterte assumed the presidency.

The prosecution said P-1348’s testimony “provides evidence of [REDACTED] around July 2016 and of the climate of violence in the Philippines at the beginning of the presidential period" and is proof of a “policy to "neutralize" alleged criminals “through violent crimes."

“The associated material for P-1348, which the prosecution seeks to introduce into evidence, forms an integral part of his Prior Recorded Testimony. These items are also necessary to fully comprehend the witness’s account, as she uses and explains them in his statement,” the filing stated.

The filing also contains references in two witnesses’ statements to Duterte’s alleged association with the Davao Death Squad and drug cartels, the targeting of mayors who did not support him, the alleged use of public funds to make payments, and his public call for drug users to register in barangays.
Dispute over admissions of testimonies
In a separate filing reported on Tuesday, Duterte’s defense opposed the prosecution’s bid to admit the recorded testimonies of witnesses P-1393 and P-1416 without requiring them to testify live.

“The Defense supports the use of Rule 68(2)(b) to expedite the trial, particularly in light of Mr. Duterte’s age and frailty. However, procedural efficiency must not come at the expense of his fundamental right to defend himself effectively,” the defense said.

Meanwhile, the Common Legal Representatives of the Victims (CLRV), asked Trial Chamber III to grant the prosecution’s request to admit the statements of witnesses P-1370, P-1393, and P-1416 under Rule 68(2)(b).

The victims’ representatives, Atty. Gilbert Andres, Atty. Joel Butuyan, and Paolina Massidda, described the testimonies and related documents as “relevant, reliable, probative, and corroborative”, adding that their admission would not prejudice Duterte’s rights.
According to the CLRV, the testimonies do not primarily concern Duterte’s personal acts and conduct, but rather the broader context of the alleged crimes against humanity.

The filing said the witnesses’ evidence principally concerns alleged extrajudicial killings in Central Luzon and an alleged policy of killing people suspected of involvement in drug-related activities.
Their admission, the CLRV said, would “serve the interests of justice” by expediting the proceedings and conserving the court’s time and resources.
The filing also stressed the interests and well-being of victims and witnesses.
The CLRV said the three witnesses are connected to grave acts of violence and killings, although much of that portion of the public filing remains redacted.

They argued that admitting the recorded testimonies would be consistent with the ICC’s duty to protect the “safety, physical and psychological well-being, dignity and privacy of victims and witnesses.”
The defense did not oppose admitting P-1370’s statement.
On November 2, the chamber will convene for the final status conference with the prosecution, defense, and victims’ representatives.
Duterte’s trial on crimes against humanity charges stemming from the killings during his anti-drug campaign is scheduled to begin on November 30. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah detained after court orders news site's closure
articles.summary: Amnesty International said the verdict against Attalah and independent outlet Mada Masr represented "a crushing blow to press freedom".

blocks.text: The editor-in-chief of the independent Egyptian news outlet Mada Masr has been taken into custody after a court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website and ordered its closure, her lawyers say.

Lina Attalah will be held until she pays the fine of 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100) also handed down by the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court. It was the maximum possible penalty for the charge, which she had rejected.
The human rights group Amnesty International said the verdict represented "a crushing blow to press freedom".
It comes only weeks after six journalists working for the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh were charged with belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.
Egypt is among the top jailers of journalists globally, with 25 currently behind bars, according to the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ).

President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi has overseen what human rights groups say is an unprecedented crackdown on dissent since he led the military's overthrow of his predecessor, Muslim Brotherhood leader Mohammed Morsi, in 2013.
Tens of thousands of people have been detained, mainly Brotherhood officials and supporters but also leading secular and liberal activists, media workers and academics.
The CPJ said Mada Masr, which was founded in 2013, was a vital source of critical reporting in Egypt and that it had long faced pressure from authorities over its journalism.

The site had repeatedly sought an operating licence from the Supreme Media Regulatory Council (SMRC) since a new media law was passed in 2018, but that its applications were either rejected or left unanswered, the media watchdog added.
Amnesty International said Lina Attalah had also faced "years of harassment and intimidation", including six criminal investigations over Mada Masr's reporting.
Last week, prosecutors summoned her for questioning over allegations of publishing "false news" and operating a website without a licence.

Mada Masr's lawyer said the investigation included a recent report that the website had published about a wave of protests in prisons across the country, as well as a letter from the SMRC regarding its legal status.
Attalah was released on bail and later referred to trial before the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court on the charge of operating a website without a licence.

During Tuesday's hearing, Judge Mohammed Mubarak ordered the courtroom to be cleared of everyone except Attalah, her eight-person defence team, and Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), an independent human rights group.

Bahgat told AFP news agency that security personnel then filed in before the judge announced that the court was denying several procedural requests made by the defence and appointing its own lawyer for Attalah.

"In a move that astonished all those present, the judge recorded in the official court minutes that the court had appointed a lawyer from the Lawyers' Syndicate to represent the defence," he said. "Lina herself spoke up to object to this lawyer being appointed to represent her, which the judge refused to record in the court minutes.
"In an even more shocking turn, the judge proceeded to dictate motions on behalf of this lawyer - who had not uttered a single word - and entered them into the official record," he added.
The judge then announced the fine for Attalah and ordered Mada Masr's closure "amid shouts and protests from the defence", before she was detained, according to Bahgat.
Amnesty International warned that the court's verdict marked "a dark day for independent journalism" in Egypt and demanded that it be overturned.

"This draconian ruling is the culmination of years of relentless harassment and unjust proceedings designed to shut down one of the country's last remaining independent media voices," said the group's senior director for regional impact, Yasmine Ahmed.
"Lina Attalah should never have been prosecuted for exercising her right to freedom of expression and doing her journalistic job."

CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah said: "If Egypt can put in custody one of its most respected editors and shut down her newsroom, no independent journalist in the country is safe. Attalah must be released immediately, and Mada Masr must be allowed to keep reporting."
