articles.title: Oleshky truce appears to hold as two European leaders have ‘frank’ call with Putin
articles.summary: Frontline near Russian-occupied city in southern Ukraine quiet for first time in years ahead of planned evacuation

blocks.text: A local ceasefire in a southern Ukrainian city under Russian occupation appeared to be holding on Tuesday, with both sides ceasing drone attacks, ahead of an apparent evacuation of about 2,000 trapped and desperate civilians.

The temporary truce began at 3am in Russian-controlled Oleshky. The city sits on the Dnipro River and is about 3 miles from Kherson, a larger city on the opposite bank. Ukrainian troops recaptured Kherson in autumn 2022.

Witnesses reported that the deadly frontline across the river was quiet for the first time in four years. The pause in fighting is due to last until 11pm on Sunday, Ukrainian officials said, and represents a significant if limited moment of de-escalation.

Finland’s president, Alexander Stubb, and Norway’s prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre, held what they described as a “frank and substantive” phone call with Vladimir Putin about efforts to end the war in Ukraine. Støre indicated afterwards that big differences remained.

The two Nordic leaders said the call – a rare instance of direct contact between Putin and western leaders – was linked to upcoming talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US, expected to take place in Abu Dhabi next month.

The ceasefire in Oleshky appears to be an attempt by the Kremlin to curry favour with Donald Trump ahead of the trilateral meeting and next week’s US midterm elections. The first lady, Melania Trump, requested the humanitarian mission, the White House has said, and an evacuation is due to begin on Thursday or Friday. Calls for a ceasefire had also been issued by Pope Leo XIV, the United Nations, EU officials and the Council of Europe.

blocks.caption: People board a bus in Kherson during a local ceasefire on Tuesday. Photograph: Evgeniy Maloletka/AP

blocks.text: Between 1,500 and 2,000 people in the city have been living under a complete blockade by Russia. The last delivery of food to stores was in May, and many people are now starving and eating weeds. The Ukrainian military has airdropped food using drones. Locals say Russian security forces detain anyone who takes it.

Russian soldiers have mined roads and use ruined buildings to coordinate round-the-clock strikes against Kherson. Some Oleshky residents have managed to escape, walking or cycling past bodies lying on the street and the burnt-out shells of numerous vehicles.

Ukrainian observers say the Kremlin is planning a major propaganda tour this week in which Kyiv is blamed for Oleshky’s destruction. Trump-supporting US media channels have been invited to witness the evacuation, in which buses will take residents to occupied Crimea and Russia.

The ceasefire does not extend to other parts of Ukraine. Overnight, Russia bombarded Kyiv with drones and ballistic missiles, killing at least one person and injuring 15. It hit a university campus, wounding students, as well as a bridge over the Dnipro and metro infrastructure. Ten other regions came under fire.

blocks.caption: A building damaged by an overnight Russian missile strike in Kyiv. Photograph: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters

blocks.text: The bridge remains closed to traffic, with some commuters walking across it to get to work. Writing on social media, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia “must stop dragging out this war” and said he welcomed European attempts to end it.

He said Stubb and Støre had briefed him on their call with Putin. “Alex and Jonas clearly conveyed to the Russian leadership the need for genuine steps towards de-escalation, particularly when it comes to our energy sector and infrastructure,” Zelenskyy wrote.
after newsletter promotion

The Finnish-Norwegian initiative comes amid growing efforts by some European nations to establish a direct channel of communication with Moscow and secure a stronger European voice in negotiations. Stubb and Støre said they took part in the call as leaders of their respective countries and were not speaking on behalf of Europe as a whole.

European governments remain divided over whether direct engagement with Putin is worthwhile, at a time when Russia’s maximalist demands remain stubbornly unchanged. There is little agreement on who should lead such talks. Stubb is seen by some EU officials as a potential candidate.

blocks.caption: (L-r) Alexander Stubb, Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Jonas Gahr Støre in Oslo on 20 October. Photograph: Heiko Junge/EPA

blocks.text: The divisions were laid bare shortly after news of the call emerged, when Denmark’s prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, criticised the move. “I am very sceptical about this independent initiative by Norway and Finland. It was not agreed with any of us,” Frederiksen said.

She added: “I see no signs that Russia wants peace with Europe – neither in the hybrid warfare it wages every day, nor in Ukraine, where brutal and aggressive strikes continue daily, claiming many lives.”

Earlier this month Putin said he was willing to resume peace negotiations but only on Russia’s hardline terms. They include the handover of the entire eastern Donbas region, including parts Russia has been unable to seize since 2014, as well as further territory in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia provinces.

Last week Zelenskyy said he was open to a peace agreement that would freeze the war along the current frontlines. “Yes, we are ready to stop this war as soon as possible,” he said in an interview with ABC News. He made clear that Ukraine would not recognise land seized and occupied by Russia as Russian.

articles.title: Palace defends budget insertions for Sandro
articles.summary: Malacañang yesterday defended insertions in the version of the P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027 approved by the House of Representatives, saying there is nothing wrong with them as long…

blocks.text: October 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines —Malacañang yesterday defended insertions in the version of the P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027 approved by the House of Representatives, saying there is nothing wrong with them as long as they benefit the public.

Palace press officer Claire Castro made the assertion when asked to comment on presidential son, House Majority Leader Sandro Marcos’ P4-billion budget for his district’s public works projects under the House General Appropriations Bill (GAB).

“If a congressman’s projects are well-executed and the allocated funds are used properly, who would oppose this, especially when these funds are sufficient to improve a district,” Castro said at a press briefing in Cagayan de Oro City.

“So, regardless of who the congressman is, as long as the funds allocated to their district are used properly – with no ghost projects and no substandard materials – there shouldn’t be any issues. An insertion is not inherently bad. It only becomes problematic when the funds are inserted into the politician’s own pocket – that is what is wrong,” she added.

Budget watchdog People’s Budget Coalition (PBC) said the House-approved 2027 version of next year’s budget contains “red flag” levels of insertions worth over P1 trillion, including around 7,000 infrastructure projects totaling P190 billion.

Marcos topped the list of Department of Public Works and Highways projects “inserted” in the House GAB, with 405 projects worth P4.37 billion going to the 1st district of Ilocos Norte, the group said.
According to PBC’s Kenneth Isaiah, the lawmakers “padded” numerous infrastructure projects without any details.

In the House version, the DPWH budget for multi-purpose buildings and access roads and bridges was augmented by P43 billion, Abante told the Senate committee on finance on Monday. – Delon Porcalla, Bella Cariaso

articles.title: PCG begins 5-day heightened alert tomorrow for Undas 2026
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard will be on heightened alert starting tomorrow until Nov. 3, amid the expected influx of passengers as the country marks All Saints’and All Souls’ Days.

blocks.text: October 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) will be on heightened alert starting tomorrow until Nov. 3, amid the expected influx of passengers as the country marks All Saints’and All Souls’ Days.
In a radio interview, PCG spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said passengers this year are expected to reach two million, higher than last year’s total of 1.5 million.
“To ensure the safety and security of our passengers, we will be placing all our Coast Guard security units nationwide in heightened alert status from Oct. 29 until Nov. 3,” Cayabyab said.
She said at least 17,000 PCG personnel will be deployed nationwide.
“We will set up passenger assistance desks. If someone has a question, we will be able to answer. And in case of any medical assistance, we will be able to respond,” Cayabyab added.
She said the PCG will have strict departure inspections and would ensure that there will be no overloading of ships.
Cayabyab added that K-9 dogs would be deployed to assist in the baggage inspection.
Lifeguards will be deployed to ensure the safety of tourists.
Over 72,000 police officers are securing Undas in coordination with the Armed Forces of the Philippines, Bureau of Fire Protection, PCG and other stakeholders.
To ensure that all police personnel are available for deployment, the Philippine National Police (PNP) will go on full alert status from Oct. 30 to Nov. 2.

On the directive of PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., police commanders have strengthened patrols along major highways, accident-prone roads and routes leading to cemeteries and transportation hubs.
Nartatez ordered police chiefs to coordinate with local government units and traffic authorities, as well as increase visibility along major travel routes.
2 million at North Cemetery
Around two million people are expected to visit the Manila North Cemetery, its director, Daniel Tan, said.
“For Undas, we expect this whole week, more or less, we will reach two million,” Tan told GMA News.
Today is the last day of interment, and all types of vehicles will be prohibited from entering the cemetery tomorrow till Monday.
Provincial bus trips
The provincial bus trips for the anticipated long weekend is enough, Provincial Bus Operators Association of the Philippines (PBOAP) executive director Alex Yague said.
Yague said there are a lot of vacant seats, noting that 1,100 buses were issued with special permits to operate beyond their routes.
“The buses right now have a lot of vacant seats. Just in case passengers will flock, there are a lot of buses that were issued special permits,” Yague told The STAR.
He noted they are expecting a lot of passengers going to provinces due to the better weather conditions compared to last year.
Yague advised the public to book their tickets online. – Emmanuel Tupas, Josiah Antonio, Rhodina Villanueva

articles.title: Defense wants 2 witnesses to testify in person vs Duterte
articles.summary: The defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte has opposed the admission of prior recorded testimony of two witnesses that the prosecution wants to introduce in the crimes against humanity case…

blocks.text: October 28, 2026 | 12:00am

In a 12-page filing dated Oct. 26, defense lawyer Peter Haynes said the defense finds it necessary for witnesses P-1416 and P-1393 to testify in person instead of their prior recorded testimonies being admitted under Rule 68(2)(b).
AFP / Pool / Piroschka Van De Wouw

MANILA, Philippines — The defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte has opposed the admission of prior recorded testimony of two witnesses that the prosecution wants to introduce in the crimes against humanity case at the International Criminal Court (ICC).
The rule allows the admission of a prior recorded testimony of a witness, who will no longer be required to appear during trial.
According to Haynes, the defense must be allowed to cross-examine both witnesses as their testimonies cover Duterte’s acts and conduct in relation to the alleged crimes.
Based on the prosecution’s earlier filing, the prior recorded testimony of P-1416 covers specific incidents related to some drug war killings.
His testimony is supposedly “relevant to the policy to ‘neutralize’ through violent crimes, including murder, alleged criminals in the Philippines,” the prosecution said.
Witness P-1393, meanwhile, was present during a police operation in San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan, where one alleged drug user was killed.

“lthough P-1393 did not witness the killing (redacted), he heard gunshots and was told by his neighbors, who were afraid to testify about what they saw, that the police officers who killed (redacted) first spoke to him and (redacted) to the barangay,” the prosecution filing read.

The prosecution argued that the prior recorded testimonies of the two witnesses may be accepted under Rule 68(2)(b) as these are “cumulative to, and corroborative of, evidence to be provided” by other witnesses who will testify in person.
But the defense argued that the testimonies relate to issues that are “materially in dispute” and that the witnesses should be presented in person to allow the defense to cross-examine them.
Duterte’s crimes against humanity trial is set to begin on Nov. 30.

articles.title: Weak peso may push up fuel, power costs
articles.summary: The peso sliding to record lows against the dollar could squeeze household budgets and threatens to push electricity bills and fuel prices even higher.

blocks.text: October 28, 2026 | 12:00am
Energy Secretary Sharon Garin, on the sidelines of the Singapore International Energy Week, warned that the weakening peso could drive up the cost of imported coal, diesel and liquefied natural gas.
Rattanakun Thongbun via Canva Pro
SINGAPORE – The peso sliding to record lows against the dollar could squeeze household budgets and threatens to push electricity bills and fuel prices even higher.
This could put further upward pressure on domestic energy prices, particularly electricity rates, amid the ongoing global oil crisis and the looming El Niño threat.
The local currency breached the 64-per-dollar mark for the first time in intraday trading yesterday, extending its string of record lows.
The Department of Energy (DOE) is exploring possible measures to cushion the impact of the peso depreciation and continued market volatility.
Garin said she would meet with Energy Regulatory Commission chairman and CEO Francis Saturnino Juan to discuss possible regulations to prevent sudden spikes in electricity bills.
The weakening peso has already contributed to higher electricity rates this month in Metro Manila and nearby provinces, as some power supply contracts are dollar-denominated.
At the pumps, the DOE is considering the staggered implementation of price adjustments to help ease the burden on motorists.
“We’ll ask them (oil companies) again once we see the computations this week. Normally, they follow, but hopefully, it won’t be necessary anymore,” Garin said.
For this week, the DOE prescribed maximum price hikes of P1.20 per liter for diesel and P0.50 per liter for kerosene.
Gasoline prices, meanwhile, went down by at least P0.30 per liter.

articles.title: No economic retaliation vs China – Palace
articles.summary: The Philippines is not inclined to resort to economic retaliation against China amid heated exchanges between Philippine officials and the Chinese embassy, Malacañang said on Tuesday,…

blocks.text: October 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines is not inclined to resort to economic retaliation against China amid heated exchanges between Philippine officials and the Chinese embassy, Malacañang said on Tuesday, stressing that the government would continue to pursue diplomatic channels.
Palace press officer Claire Castro said the Marcos administration maintains that trade and investment relations with China should be separate from the country’s efforts to defend its maritime rights.

“That is not how our President thinks. The President does not approach the issue like children who are quarreling. The President and the administration are negotiating and engaging in discussions with the leadership of other countries through diplomatic channels,” Castro said at a media briefing in Cagayan de Oro City when asked whether the government was considering a retaliatory ban on nickel or other products from Surigao del Sur to China.
Castro maintained that the Philippines and China continue to cooperate in areas related to the economy, trade and investment.
“The President would not consider that kind of retaliation, as we know that China and the Philippines are helping each other in areas related to the economy, trade and investment,” she said.
An Oct. 22 report by Chinese media said Beijing was planning to impose sanctions on Filipino lawmakers over their alleged anti-China remarks.

Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry Inc. president Victor Lim earlier urged government officials to reconsider plans to impose sanctions on Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan, warning that retaliation from Beijing could further harm the Philippine economy.
Tarriela faces cyberlibel raps

Amid the tensions over China policy and the West Philippine Sea, former national security adviser Clarita Carlos has filed a cyberlibel complaint against Philippine Coast Guard spokesman for the West Philippine Sea Jay Tarriela and Philippine Military Academy Superintendent Lt. Gen. Michael Logico.
The complaint followed a public exchange between Carlos and Tarriela over their positions on China and the West Philippine Sea.
Carlos had criticized Tarriela’s public statements, calling him a “troublemaker” and urging him to stop speaking publicly.

Tarriela responded in a social media post, questioning Carlos’ record as national security adviser and accusing her of failing to do enough to defend Philippine maritime rights during her tenure. – Mark Ernest Villeza

articles.title: Dizon, Lopez: Minimal personnel changes
articles.summary: o maintain momentum, returning Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon and incoming Public Works Secretary Giovanni Lopez vowed that personnel movement in their respective departments will be kept to a…

blocks.text: October 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — To maintain momentum, returning Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon and incoming Public Works Secretary Giovanni Lopez vowed that personnel movement in their respective departments will be kept to a bare minimum.

Dizon said he will not bring Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) DPWH personnel over to the Department of Transportation (DOTr) and vowed to keep existing technical teams intact to preserve continuity.
Lopez agreed, stating that major personnel overhauls at this juncture would be counterproductive to the administration’s targets.
“The President’s instruction is for us to continue each agency’s respective projects and accelerate them. Any major structural changes at this point would be quite counterproductive,” Lopez said.

Dizon and Lopez said they would soon conduct joint site inspections, including newly rehabilitated facilities such as the Siargao Airport terminal ahead of a major international surfing event next week.
‘Focus on work’
Dizon and Lopez vowed faster implementation of key infrastructure projects during a joint press conference at the DPWH Multipurpose Hall yesterday.
Dizon downplayed concerns that the Cabinet position swap ordered by President Marcos would derail ongoing structural and system upgrades in both infrastructure agencies.

“It will even be faster, because first of all, Sec. Banoy (Lopez) is more capable than I am. He truly understands the systems,” Dizon said, noting that the root issues plaguing the public works department are fundamentally structural rather than isolated individual wrongdoings.
Dizon cautioned those expecting a relaxed regime at the DPWH under a new chief.
He warned the DPWH staff about his successor’s work ethic, noting that Lopez wakes up even earlier than he does to send work message.
Dizon urged department officials and the public to move past political gossip and focus on addressing national issues.
Lopez said the job swap between him and Dizon was a surprise to him, but stressed that he did not dare question the President’s move.
“I did not ask why,” Lopez said.
Airport, rail upgrades
Lopez expressed confidence that Dizon would push the envelope in his return to the DOTr, which is set to finish airport and railway upgrades before the end of the Marcos administration in 2028.
Lopez wants to see Dizon finish the new passenger terminal building of the Sayak Airport in Siargao to expand its seating capacity to 750.

Lopez said Dizon must keep up the pressure in building the Central Mindanao Airport in Cotabato. The project, after several delays, aims to improve trade and tourism in the central provinces of Mindanao.
Lopez also asked Dizon to hold San Miguel Corp. (SMC) accountable to its promise of partially operating the MRT-7 next year. – Elijah Felice Rosales, Josiah Antonio

articles.title: 'Jinggoy had P7.4 billion in congressional initiatives’
articles.summary: Sen. Jinggoy Estrada had at least P7.4 billion in “congressional initiatives” in the 2025 budget, which had been approved for funding, public works chief-turned-state witness Manuel…

blocks.text: October 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Jinggoy Estrada had at least P7.4 billion in “congressional initiatives” in the 2025 budget, which had been approved for funding, public works chief-turned-state witness Manuel Bonoan testified yesterday before the Sandiganbayan.
The anti-graft court’s Fifth Division is hearing the petition for bail filed by Estrada for his P573-million plunder case involving alleged kickbacks from flood control projects.
Aside from the P7.4 billion, Estrada also had P475 million worth of infrastructure projects in the 2025 budget shared with a lawmaker, Bonoan said.

Additionally, the suspended senator also requested for a P1-billion “Senate leadership fund,” which was coursed through then-Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) undersecretary Roberto Bernardo, according to the former agency chief.

Bonoan said Bernardo submitted to him the list of Estrada’s requested projects. He said the late DPWH undersecretary Catalina Cabral initially recommended P500 million to be included in the department’s proposed budget for 2025.

“After the inclusion of P500 million, Usec. Bernardo requested an additional P500 million since Sen. Estrada is already Senate President Pro Tempore. They are still asking for additional P500 million for the availment of the Senate leadership fund,” Bonoan said.
Bonoan said Estrada made the additional request of P500 million to allegedly help cover his election expenses.

Estrada, however, did not run for election in 2025 since he was still serving his six-year term as senator, but it was his wife Precy who ran for a House seat in the 2025 polls as first nominee of BFF party-list.
Bonoan acknowledged he never spoke to Estrada directly regarding his requests but relied mainly on what Bernardo told him and that the project list did not bear the signature of Estrada.
He, however, alleged that the suspended senator asked for a 25 percent commitment fee from the funding of the projects.
Of the P1 billion, only P700 million was approved for funding under the 2025 General Appropriations Act.
Bonoan said he was sure that it was the senator who requested the projects, citing Estrada and Bernardo’s close friendship.
“I do not have any reason to doubt because I know the good senator and Usec Bernardo are very good friends,” he told the court.
He said Bernardo used to serve as district engineer for DPWH’s Manila office during the term of Estrada’s father, former president Joseph Estrada, as Manila mayor.
P5 billion in kickbacks for Alcantara

Meanwhile, Carlo Rivera of the DPWH Bulacan 1st District Engineering Office said he delivered at least P5 billion worth of commitment fees or kickbacks he collected from contractors to his boss, former DPWH Bulacan District Engineer Henry Alcantara.
The amount, he said, is equivalent to 25 percent of the cost of Bulacan infrastructure projects from 2022 to 2025.
Rivera said the money was ultimately delivered to then House appropriations panel chair Zaldy Co, who then distributed it to project proponents.
These include Bernardo, Estrada and former senator Ramon Revilla Jr.
Rivera said Alcantara forwarded the list of proponents for flood control projects and merely relayed the information to him.

Additionally, the 25 percent commitments were a portion of the cost of Bulacan infrastructure projects, which totaled P519 million in 2022, P12.93 billion in 2023, P14.19 billion in 2024 and P7.385 billion in 2025, Rivera noted.
He also told the anti-graft court that the commitment fees from contractors were tagged under Co’s name, and that he was the one contacting the contractors for commitment fees.
He also claimed he frequently accompanied contractors who delivered cash to Alcantara.
These contractors include: Topnotch Catalyst Builders, ARL Builders, Wawao Builders, IM Construction Corp. and SYMS Construction Trading.
Rivera said he was tasked by Alcantara to collect the commitment fees from 2022 to 2025.
He said he personally followed up and collected cash commitments from contractors, counted the money and marked the amounts on post-it notes before the funds were turned over to Alcantara.
Rivera testified that former speaker Martin Romualdez was not among the proponents of flood control projects, from which kickbacks were allegedly collected.
Rivera was suspended from his post from September 2025 to March 2026 and is currently on floating status.

articles.title: Justice who penned Imelda acquittal may be next CJ?
articles.summary: As rumors swirled about President Marcos’ choice for the next chief justice, Malacañang urged the public to just wait for the announcement, noting that all the candidates are qualified.

blocks.text: October 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — As rumors swirled about President Marcos’ choice for the next chief justice, Malacañang urged the public to just wait for the announcement, noting that all the candidates are qualified.

The statement was issued amid speculative reports that the President would pick Supreme Court (SC) Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda, who penned the decision that reversed the conviction on seven counts of graft of Marcos’ mother Imelda.

“Regarding the President’s choice of the next chief justice of the Supreme Court, we do not want to preempt the President’s decision. We can expect that whoever is chosen, while all of them are highly competent, will naturally be someone who stands out,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said when asked if Marcos would pick Zalameda.
Castro also denied reports that she would be appointed associate justice.
“Associate Justice of the Supreme Court? Auntie Claire? I didn’t apply. So there is no truth to that,” she said.
The Judicial and Bar Council has concluded its interviews of candidates for the next chief justice and is expected to submit a short list of nominees to Marcos.
SC Associate Justices Zalameda, Japar Dimaampao and Jose Midas Marquez were interviewed by the JBC on the second and final day of the interviews.

Transitional justice lawyer Ruben Carranza expressed concern about the selection of Zalameda, saying it could further undermine public confidence in the justice system following the SC’s acquittal of Imelda Marcos. Carranza, a former commissioner of the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG), also criticized the President’s statements on the Marcos family’s alleged ill-gotten wealth.

Carranza said the President’s claims raised concerns about his credibility as he prepares to appoint the country’s next top magistrate. “Marcos Jr.’s lying is in character,” Carranza told “Storycon” on One News, referring to the President’s statements about cases involving his family’s wealth. Carranza questioned the SC’s decision reversing Imelda Marcos’ 2018 graft conviction, saying it contradicted a 2003 ruling that ordered the forfeiture of $680 million in Swiss bank deposits linked to the Marcoses.
Zalameda is pushing for respect for the principle of separation of powers by each branch of government, saying the high tribunal should not exercise powers that belong to the political branches.
Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen and Associate Justice Benjamin Caguiao were interviewed on Oct. 22.
The post will be vacated by Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo who will compulsory retire on Nov. 6 at the age of 70.

During his interview, Zalameda said the next chief justice should lead through service and accountability and ensure that the judiciary remains responsive to the needs of the public and its personnel.
He said effective leadership is about serving others and enabling them to perform their duties effectively.

“The role is to create an environment where problems are heard, solutions are developed, good ideas are supported and people are given the tools to fulfill their responsibilities. Leadership is ultimately about service, accountability and enabling others to succeed,” he said.
He also said the judiciary should strengthen its anti-corruption initiatives, address allegations of misconduct, and protect those who report wrongdoing.
The next chief justice, however, must not hesitate to act when a constitutional question properly comes before the high court.

He said public officials involved in the hike in unprogrammed funds in the 2024 and 2025 national budgets, which the high court has since declared as unconstitutional, should be presumed to have acted in good faith unless proven otherwise.

He added that unprogrammed funds remain constitutional and that official acts are presumed valid unless declared otherwise by a competent court. “When you say it is constitutional, I don’t think the public officers may be held liable for such act, which is declared constitutional,” he said. “Aside from that, there is presumption of regularity on the part of these public officials and all their acts are considered valid until such acts are declared invalid,” Zalameda added.

He clarified that the SC did not rule on the possible liability of public officials who authored and implemented these budgets because the issue was not among those raised before it. He also pointed out that the SC has the authority to review acts of Congress and the executive branch but should not interfere with every government decision simply because another course of action might be preferable.

“Each branch of government is bound by its own constitutional mandate. Respect for these boundaries is one of the foundations of a constitutional government,” Zalameda said. In a recent ruling, the high tribunal declared as unconstitutional Congress’ P449.5-billion increase in unprogrammed appropriations under the 2024 General Appropriations Act (GAA) and the P17.99-billion increase in the Special Road Fund under the 2025 GAA. It also struck down certain provisions governing the release of unprogrammed appropriations under the 2026 GAA. However, the SC upheld the constitutionality of unprogrammed appropriations as a budgetary mechanism, subject to constitutional safeguards. Zalameda was appointed to his post at the SC by former president Rodrigo Duterte in August 2019. He penned the 50-page SC ruling that overturned the conviction by the Sandiganbayan of former first lady Imelda Marcos on seven counts of graft involving her alleged financial interests in private foundations in Switzerland.
For his part, Marquez committed to institutionalize the SC’s digital transformation blueprint if he gets appointed as chief justice.

He would also push to further strengthen the Court’s communications and public relations to keep the public informed about what is happening inside the courthouses and foster a legal system that is fair, transparent and accountable to the public.

During the interviews, JBC member Sen. Francis Pangilinan asked the candidates whether the judiciary failed in the fight against corruption, citing controversies involving the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) and flood control projects scams.
Zalameda said corruption, while not the sole responsibility of the judiciary, is a concern that must be addressed by all branches of the government.
If appointed as chief justice, he said he will form a group that would monitor the stages of the cases involving these graft and corruption cases.

“This monitoring group will have to report to me from arraignment to judgment,” he said. Dimaampao, meanwhile, vowed to strengthen accountability in the judiciary and to remind judges of their constitutional duties.

“I will be guided by fiat justitia ruat caelum, let justice be done though the heavens fall,” he said. Marquez said continued digital monitoring of cases through the judiciary’s electronic court system could help address delays in the resolution of cases. Asked what the public could expect from him if he becomes the first Muslim chief justice in the country, Dimaampao said he will be remembered as someone who “upheld the supremacy of the Constitution, defended and protected the independence of the judiciary and ensured that justice was served without fear or favor.”
Not ill-gotten?

During a luncheon meeting with members of the Foreign Correspondents Association of the Philippines last Aug. 14, Marcos defended his family’s assets, claiming they are “not ill-gotten.” Carranza said the 2003 ruling had established that the deposits were ill-gotten wealth, while the more recent decision found that Imelda Marcos’ actions did not constitute the offense for which she had been convicted. “Imagine that, a President who lies about cases that were decided against him will now be the one appointing a chief justice who might be the same person who ruled on the innocence of Imelda Marcos,” Carranza said. He urged Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla to consider seeking a review of the ruling by the SC en banc, or the full court, if legally permissible.– Mark Ernest Villeza

articles.title: JV open to inviting budget watchdogs to bicam hearings
articles.summary: Senate finance committee chairman JV Ejercito is open to inviting civil society organizations to the bicameral conference committee hearings on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027,…

blocks.text: October 28, 2026 | 12:00am
Senate finance committee chairman JV Ejercito
Jesse Bustos / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — Senate finance committee chairman JV Ejercito is open to inviting civil society organizations (CSOs) to the bicameral conference committee hearings on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, after the groups flagged up to P1 trillion in potential pork barrel funds in the House of Representatives’ version of the spending bill.

During a public consultation on Monday, the People’s Budget Coalition flagged P695 billion in “hard pork” for “politicized infrastructure,” P210 billion in “soft pork” for “patronage-driven ayuda” and P112 billion in “shadow pork” tucked into unprogrammed appropriations.

Before the hearing adjourned, Sen. Panfilo Lacson invited the groups to participate in the bicameral conference committee hearings, where lawmakers reconcile conflicting provisions in the House and Senate versions of the General Appropriations Bill.
“Without you, we can’t do it. Our staff is good but we can’t comb all the items in the budget. You are our multiplier effect,” Lacson told the CSO representatives.
Aside from the alleged discretionary funds, the proposed allocation for the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth) were also flagged by certain health groups.
Dr. Alberto Ong, co-convenor of the Health Professionals Alliance After COVID-19, warned that PhilHealth’s proposed P74.4-billion allocation was inadequate to meet Filipinos’ health care needs.

“This amount is projected to sustain PhilHealth only until approximately March 2027. And after that, the burden of health care costs will increasingly fall on patients themselves... This is not an isolated budgetary shortfall. The chronic underfunding of PhilHealth represents a continuing failure to fulfill the government’s obligations under the Universal Health Care Act,” Ong said.

The groups urged the Senate to increase PhilHealth’s subsidy to between P244 billion and P376 billion to expand benefits and help direct and indirect contributors pay for medical expenses after the subsidy was reduced from P129.8 billion in 2026 to P74.4 billion in the executive’s proposed 2027 budget.

The House did not increase the allocation, opting instead to nearly double the budget for the Department of Health’s Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) program to P49.2 billion from P24 billion.

Action for Economic Reforms health team official Paula Mae Tanquieng, a counsel for petitioners in the Supreme Court case involving the impounded PhilHealth funds, criticized the decision to expand discretionary medical assistance while leaving PhilHealth inadequately funded.

“While PhilHealth faces a massive funding gap, the House continues to expand discretionary medical assistance programs, when we are told that there is not enough money for PhilHealth,” she said” - Rhodina Villanueva

articles.title: Bato urges SC anew to block arrest
articles.summary: Amid the one-week ultimatum issued by the Philippine National Police (PNP) for him to surrender and the P50-million bounty placed on his head, Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa has urged the…

blocks.text: October 28, 2026 | 12:00am
Photo taken in 2022 shows Sen. Ronald dela Rosa with his wife Nancy, who pleaded for the ‘powerful few’ to come to his aid amid a closing window for his surrender.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — Amid the one-week ultimatum issued by the Philippine National Police (PNP) for him to surrender and the P50-million bounty placed on his head, Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa has urged the Supreme Court (SC) anew to prevent his arrest.

In a 15-page manifestation filed with the SC yesterday, Dela Rosa, through counsel Israelito Torreon, petitioned the high court to reverse its May 2026 denial of the request for temporary restraining order (TRO) or status quo ante order (SQAO) against the implementation of the International Criminal Court (ICC) warrant.

Torreon cited supervening events that would warrant the SC’s grant of the request for a TRO, including the October pronouncement of PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. that the senator is considered armed and dangerous and the placement of the P50-million bounty.

The manifestation also mentioned Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla’s announcement that the government was abandoning its prior approach of negotiation, as well as Malacañang’s statement that the President had directed law enforcement authorities to act swiftly in capturing Dela Rosa.

“Taken together, these are not stray remarks of individual officials. They constitute an announced executive enforcement program all directed at the arrest of a sitting senator of the Republic for surrender to a foreign tribunal, while the legality of that very act is pending before this Honorable Court,” the manifestation read.
In its resolution last May, the high tribunal, in a vote of 9-5-1, denied Dela Rosa’s plea for TRO and/or an SQAO, ruling that the senator has “no clear and unmistakable right to be protected.”
Wife pleads for help
Meanwhile, Dela Rosa’s wife pleaded for the “powerful few” to come to his aid amid a closing window for the senator to surrender.
“I just pray that the powerful few, who were also his friends, would come to realize he is not their enemy nor the enemy of this state,” Nancy dela Rosa posted on Facebook.
Nancy appealed to these people not to use her husband for their personal agenda, adding he has not wronged them.
“He needs your help, not your persecution,” she said.
Nancy did not identify the people she was referring to in her post. - Emmanuel Tupas, Helen Flores

articles.title: Bottled water and tinned food sales surge after UK government issues emergency stockpile advice
articles.summary:
Retailers also report jump in purchases of wind-up radios and torches to deal with extreme weather and cyber-attacks

Sales of tinned foods, bottled water, wind-up radios and torches have…

blocks.text: Sales of tinned foods, bottled water, wind-up radios and torches have surged after the UK government advised households to prepare for emergencies.

Retailers have reported a jump in sales of items linked to preparation for emergencies such as extreme weather or cyber-attacks. The Be Ready campaign was launched last week with the aim of persuading households to lay in supplies to last 72 hours.
Maplin said sales of torches had almost quadrupled and sales of power banks and radios had doubled. One brand of emergency wind-up radio sold out on Friday.

The specialist technology retailer said sales would have been higher but it was low on stock, particularly for power banks after a summer of heatwaves and the fallout from the Iran war. Home security camera sales were up 130%.
Ollie Marshall, the managing director of Maplin, said: “Within hours of the Be Ready announcement we saw people reach for the basics – a torch, a wind-up radio, a power bank.
“These are simple, affordable products that keep a household connected and informed when the power goes out, and it’s encouraging to see people taking the advice seriously.”

The grocery chain Iceland said sales of tinned products were up 40% over the weekend and it had also seen strong sales of bottled water. A spokesperson said: “It’s clear consumers have listened to the government’s message. Our supplies of these products remain healthy.”
The online grocer Ocado said demand for some products was up and it would “continue to work with suppliers to ensure there is stock for customers to gradually add items to their shops”.
Several major supermarkets said they had seen no material change in demand in tinned goods and that the cooler, stormy weather was more likely to influence demand for soups and beans.

Jim Bligh, food policy director at the British Retail Consortium, said: “While some retailers have seen a small uptick in sales for some products, food availability remains strong and retailers remain well stocked with all essential products.”
The boom in interest for relatively unusual gadgets helped specialist outdoor and “prepper” sites.

Zaid Al-Mufti, founder of survival kit seller EvaQ8, said over the weekend it had sold out of items including a make of wind-up radio and water purification tablets. He said the company had sold about 300 radios compared with the usual 15.
Long-life dried food was also in high demand but Al-Mufti did not expect this to last.

“History has shown us people’s attention span doesn’t last long,” said Al-Mufti who keeps a “grab bag” with emergency gear in his car after time spent in earthquake-prone California where such precautions are normal. “The one time demand lasted was during Covid and we also saw demand when Russia invaded Ukraine.”
after newsletter promotion

Josh Pringle, co-founder of the online store Sgt Prepper, said business had been 10 to 15 times busier than usual last weekend, particularly focused on wind-up radios and long-life food including tins that last for 25 years.
“I have never seen it like this before.” he said, saying the site’s larger wind-up radio had sold out and he was having to hunt for different brands because his supplier did not have enough stock.
While the number of people buying radios and water purification tablets remains relatively low, many more households have been adding tins of food to their weekly shop.
Retail industry insiders said supermarkets had been well prepared for a surge in food and drink sales and had good supplies of the long-life groceries recommended by the government.
While pictures of empty shelves and queues have appeared on social media, industry sources warned against reading too much into the posts.

“Inevitably some people will post pictures online of an empty shelf of water, beans or other products, however the likelihood is that just out of shot is a whole load of alternatives of a different brand available for everyone,” one insider said.

articles.title: Palace to Bato dela Rosa: If conscience is clear, there should be no fear of facing ICC case
articles.summary: Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro shot back at remarks calling efforts to arrest Senator Bato Dela as "persecution."

blocks.text: Published October 27, 2026 11:43pm
Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro shot back at remarks calling efforts to arrest Senator Bato Dela as "persecution."
Castro instead urged the senator, who has been in hiding, to face his case before the International Criminal Court (ICC).
“If your conscience is clear, you should not be afraid to face the case filed before the ICC,” Castro said in a statement in Filipino.

“We will not comment on the feelings of Senator Bato Dela Rosa’s wife because we respect her situation. However, her allegation that the senator’s arrest is an act of persecution is contrary to the truth,” she added.
Castro said complaints against Dela Rosa over alleged crimes against humanity linked to the Duterte administration’s bloody war on drugs had been raised as early as 2017.
Castro also urged the public to remember the victims of alleged extrajudicial killings (EJKs), including poor people who were killed and allegedly had evidence planted against them.
She called for justice for those who were killed, oppressed and abused during the campaign.
“If no killings had occurred in connection with the EJKs, former President Rodrigo Duterte’s co-perpetrators would have no case to face before the ICC today,” Castro said.

Bato is in hiding after the International Criminal Court (ICC) issued a warrant of arrest for him on November 6, 2025 in connection with the crimes against humanity case involving former President Rodrigo Duterte.
On Tuesday, his wife Nancy dela Rosa thanked her husband's supporters and said he is not the enemy of his friends and of the country.
"Thank you for helping me realize that there are millions who still believe and support him," Nancy said in a post on Facebook.
"I just pray that the powerful few who were also his friends would come to realize he is not their enemy nor the enemy of this state," she said.
Nancy also appealed to those in power not to use Bato for their personal agenda.
"Pls do not use him for your personal agenda. He has helped you in countless ways and he has done you no wrong personally. He needs your help, not your persecution," she added.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: West warns of famine risk in Sudan as civil war grinds on
articles.summary: Millions face acute hunger in Sudan as conflict, drought and funding cuts aggravate the humanitarian crisis.

blocks.text: The US and 30 other Western states have warned of an "alarming deterioration" in food security in Sudan, urging the warring sides in the civil war to remove obstacles to humanitarian aid to prevent famine.
In a joint statement, the signatories said conflict was the main driver of Sudan's hunger crisis, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting food production.

"There is very little to survive on," Yusuf Roble, regional director for Islamic Relief East Africa, told BBC Newsday, describing how people returning to Omdurman were finding their homes destroyed or looted.
The war, which began in April 2023, has displaced 14 million people.

The statement, external was signed by EU states, the UK, Canada, Switzerland and Norway, as well as the US, where it was published by the state department on Monday after first appearing on the European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations website.
It estimates that 19.5 million people or 41% of Sudan's population are experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity, including five million facing emergency levels of hunger.

"I met a mother of seven children who doesn't really know the whereabouts of her husband for the last three and a half years and he was the breadwinner, the sole breadwinner for the family," Roble said.

While the war in Sudan has led to what the World Health Organization has described as the world's worst humanitarian crisis, Roble said only 40% of Sudan's 2026 humanitarian needs plan had been funded as of September.
"Their meals come from the community kitchen, which doesn't really even have very long-term support because of funding cuts," Roble added.
The joint statement warns that "the number of children suffering from severe acute malnutrition could exceed the projected 825,000" without immediate action.

The crisis is being exacerbated by what the signatories describe as systematic obstruction of aid and the effects of El Niño, which has reduced rainfall and increased drought across more than half of Sudan.

"The parties to the conflict bear primary responsibility for alleviating the suffering of the Sudanese people," the statement says, urging them to lift all impediments to humanitarian assistance and allow full, safe, rapid and unimpeded access.
In June, the UN-backed Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, a measure of the severity and magnitude of food crises, estimated that 5.1 million people in Sudan faced severe hunger.
The civil war in Sudan began in April 2023 following a power struggle between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.

articles.title: Woman’s world ‘tilted on axis’ on learning husband invited men to sexually assault her, court told
articles.summary:
Four men on trial charged with sexually assaulting Joanne Young while she was sedated, restrained and blindfolded

A woman’s world was “tilted on its axis” when she discovered that for years…

blocks.text: A woman’s world was “tilted on its axis” when she discovered that for years her former husband had been drugging her and inviting men into their family home to sexually assault her while she was restrained and blindfolded, a court has been told.
Businessman Philip Young advertised his then wife, Joanne Young, on dating and swinging websites, presenting it as a “kink” for both of them, Winchester crown court heard.
In fact, he had been sedating her, plunging her into “an inanimate state” where anything could be done to her by whoever answered the adverts, jurors were told.
Young, 50, has pleaded guilty to multiple charges of abuse against his former wife, who has waived her right to anonymity.
The jury of eight men and four women is hearing the trial of four men jointly charged with sexually assaulting Joanne Young, 49.

The alleged offences carried out by the four – Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, Richard Wilkins, 62, Norman Macksoni, 48, and Mohammed Hassan, 38 – are said to have taken place between the summer of 2016 and the winter of 2023. They deny the offences.
Sarah Jones KC, prosecuting, said Joanne Young had no idea what had been happening to her when police arrived at the family home in Swindon, Wiltshire.
She said: “The world she thought she knew had entirely tilted on its axis. The relationship she thought she had appears now to be wholly unreal – she does not even know what she doesn’t know.”

Jones told jurors they were going to have to contend with “some depressingly awful and sordid material”. She told them: “You are going to see videos of things you cannot then un-see and may find you can’t forget.”
Jones said the videos that formed the bulk of the evidence showed Joanne Young was the victim of her husband’s fantasy to watch her being “crawled over” by men “plucked from the internet”.

The barrister said the case was about whether it was ever reasonable to have sex with an unknown woman without checking with her first. “Whether it is ever reasonable to think someone truly can give consent on another’s behalf,” she added.
The barrister said Joanne and Philip Young married in 2004 and had three children, now young adults. She said: “From the outside they seemed a normal couple with a normal family life.

Joanne Young characterised her sex life as “fairly normal” and was emphatic that she and her husband were “monogamous … physically and emotionally … the traditional sense of marriage … it was us two kind of till the end.” She didn’t like being out of control, not even liking to take a sleeping tablet, the prosecutor said.
The court was told her husband had some “preferences” in their sex life. He liked his wife blindfolded and with restraints, which she did not object to.

In 2015 a packet of a sedative drug that had been posted to Philip Young from India was intercepted at customs. Police visited him and he denied knowledge, telling them someone must have obtained his name through his business.

But Jones said this helped build a picture of Young searching from 2015, at least, to trace drugs that could be used on their own or with alcohol to send Joanne Young into “a deep sleep where she would be disoriented, unaware of her surroundings and unlikely to be able to recall what happened”.
In 2023 after a night out, came an indication she had that her marriage was not what she had believed, the jury heard.
While she and her husband were having sex, she “felt someone else’s hand on my wrist and it wasn’t his [her husband’s] hand”.
She said “I was obviously really shocked because, obviously you don’t expect someone else to be in your bedroom. Phil said to the person: ‘Get down,’ and the person ducked at the end of the bed.”

Joanne Young later said: “I was just really shocked. There was this man in my house and I was naked.” She hid in the bathroom. The following morning Young said he had been looking in “forums” and invited someone round the house to watch them have sex.

Jones said: “She had stumbled upon the edges of a far greater issue in her relationship. Young had advertised her on websites – he sought strangers to come and sleep with his wife – any age, any race – but as close to Swindon as possible so that when the circumstances were right they could be seized upon immediately.
The investigation began when police received a notification that the user of a social media account connected to Philip Young had uploaded extreme pornography.

Officers went to his address and they found videos of Joanne Young lying naked on her bed, restrained and blindfolded while other men engaged in sexual activity with her as her husband recorded what had taken place.

Jones told the jury that none of the defendants now suggested Joanne Young was actually consenting. She said: “Each agrees that she was not. But what each defendant is likely to say is that they believed at the time that she was consenting and to argue that such a belief was reasonable.”

The prosecutor continued: “It is their last desperate throw of the dice to convince certainly you and perhaps even themselves that they are not rapists or sexual offenders when they took what her husband was offering out to them without ever checking for a second with the woman herself whether she was OK with it.”
Young will be sentenced after this trial.
The trial continues.

articles.title: Myanmar: Is the US undermining the EU's diplomatic blockade?
articles.summary: With the US reopening talks with Myanmar's military-backed government, and several Southeast Asian countries restarting diplomatic contacts, the EU is facing uncomfortable questions about its own…

image.caption: The head of Myanmar's junta, Min Aung Hlaing, became the head of the country's nominally civilian government in April 2026Image: Aung Shine Oo/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The US government has begun a quiet reproachment with Myanmar's military-backed government, holding two rounds of talks since September, with State Department representative Michael Vance reportedly meeting Myanmar officials in Naypyitaw and then in Tokyo earlier this month.

Washington wants to tackle online scam centers, secure the release of an imprisoned American businessman Adam Castillo, and potentially gain access to Myanmar's rare-earth resources. The market for the valuable minerals is currently controlled by the US rival China.

Meanwhile, Southeast Asian governments are also increasingly questioning their policy of isolating Myanmar's military leadership, and multiple countries have already renewed direct diplomatic contacts.

The EU, however, continues to reject the legitimacy of the military junta in the war-torn country. The European bloc has also remained unmoved by the 2025/2026 election which ended with military chief Min Aung Hlaing becoming the president. The military retains control over the political system.
Human Rights Watch's Elaine Pearson on Myanmar election
EU's sanctions still in force

The EU responded to Myanmar's February 2021 military coup by suspending direct financial assistance to the government, imposing targeted sanctions and sharply reducing diplomatic engagement with the military authorities.

blocks.caption: Despite the Western boycott, junta leader Min Aung Hlaing has made official trips to India, China and Russia [FILE: June 1, 2026]Image: Manish Swarup/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Its sanctions currently cover 105 individuals and 22 entities connected to the military. In April, the EU extended these measures for another 12 months.
At the same time, Brussels is providing humanitarian assistance to displaced communities and Rohingya refugees and is supporting civil society organizations.
Thailand-Myanmar border clinic helps people fleeing war

The EU also stopped short of withdrawing Myanmar's preferential trade access because of concerns about the consequences for workers, particularly the mostly young women employed in the country's garment industry. Last year, bilateral goods trade was worth about €4 billion ($4.46 billion), up from €3.4 billion in 2019.
Brussels supports ASEAN's peace deal

The civil war triggered by the 2021 coup has killed an estimated 100,000 people. Rebel groups still control or contest large swathes of Myanmar, and over 4 million people have been internally displaced, according to UN data.
The EU "continues to uphold its policy of non-recognition of the current military regime," in view of "the ongoing violence and the attack against its own population," an EU spokesman told DW.

At the same time, the bloc "is closely monitoring developments in the discussions and positions of the United States, Japan, ASEAN countries and other major actors with representatives of Myanmar's military regime."

"It also supports ASEAN efforts, in particular the Five-Point Consensus, which has yet to be fully implemented," the spokesperson added, referring to the peace deal proposed by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in 2021.
Myanmar diplomats reach out to European partners
In the aftermath of the coup, ASEAN took the unprecedented decision to exclude Myanmar's military leaders from its highest-level meetings after the junta failed to implement the regional peace plan.

However, ASEAN's position is showing signs of change. Some member states, most notably Myanmar's neighbor Thailand, signal growing frustration with the lack of progress towards ending Myanmar's civil war.
New Thai labor scheme offers hope for Myanmar refugees

Last week, Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow welcomed Washington's renewed engagement and suggested that ASEAN members would hold substantive discussions about Myanmar's future at their summit in Manila next month.

Myanmar's authorities are also seeking to break their diplomatic isolation. In September, Myanmar's leader Hlaing gave an interview to Time magazine, his first with a major Western publication since the coup, as part of an apparent effort to rebuild relations with Western governments.

On October 22, Burma Campaign UK, a London-based human rights organization, accused the British government of making a "significant shift in approach" after the British Foreign Office hosted Win Zeyar Tun, the charge d'affaires of Myanmar's military-controlled embassy in London, at an ASEAN diplomatic gathering days earlier.

According to an article published by Intelligence Online this month, the regime's charge d'affaires in Brussels, Khin Thidar Ay, has also sought contacts with European politicians, including Czech MEP Ondrej Dostal, a member of the European Parliament's delegation for Southeast Asia.
EU's isolation 'has achieved relatively little'

Kristina Kironska, of Palacky University Olomouc in the Czech Republic and an expert on the EU's policy on Myanmar, told DW that the EU has little reason to follow Washington's apparent shift towards engagement with the Myanmar junta.
The US strategy "appears to be pursuing specific interests" such as rare earth mining and cybercrime, she said.
Thailand: Rare earth mining pollutes rivers

However, the most important rare earth mining operations are no longer controlled by the military, but by Myanmar's ethnic rebels such as the Kachin Independence Organization in Kachin State. Therefore, "it remains to be seen what the US can achieve through negotiations with the junta," she said.

The EU has long positioned itself as a defender of democracy and human rights in Myanmar, "so abandoning this now because the US is exploring a new, perhaps more transactional approach would undermine the EU's credibility," Kironska told DW.
"At the same time, isolation has achieved relatively little. The question is therefore not whether the EU should engage, but rather with whom and under what conditions," she added.
Balancing act between Myanmar's rebels and junta

The EU is forced to consider risks to its own influence. If Washington, ASEAN governments and other regional powers increase their engagement with Myanmar's authorities, the EU risks becoming increasingly marginal in discussions about the country's political future.
Yet greater engagement with the military could undermine Brussels' relations with Myanmar's democratic opposition and ethnic resistance organizations, many of which control substantial territory.

"The key question for Brussels is whether it can remain a credible defender of democratic change while ensuring that it still has a meaningful voice in the negotiations that will determine Myanmar's future," Sabe Soe, director of the NGO Burma Centre Prague, told DW.

One possibility is for Brussels to maintain its sanctions against military leaders and their businesses while expanding diplomacy through ASEAN, the UN and other regional partners, said Soe. The EU could also tie any easing of restrictions to humanitarian access, improvements in political freedoms and progress towards peace.

Soe also suggested that the EU could pursue economic engagement in areas administered by revolutionary and ethnic resistance forces, offering an alternative to engagement centred on the military authorities in Naypyidaw.
This approach would allow the EU to remain involved in Myanmar's future without necessarily recognizing its military-backed government, she said.
For now, Brussels seems to have little appetite for a fundamental policy rethink. But this could change as more governments reopen their doors to Myanmar's generals.

articles.title: Ottawa tables new MAID legislation, excluding people suffering solely from mental illness
articles.summary: Legislation tabled on Tuesday also sets criteria for people to make what's known as an "advance request" for medically assisted death, before losing the capacity to consent due to their health…

image.caption: Justice Minister Sean Fraser had said earlier this month that Ottawa decided not to move forward with plans to expand MAID access 'in circumstances where mental illness is the sole basis.' (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New

Legislation tabled on Tuesday also sets criteria for people to make what's known as an "advance request" for medically assisted death, before losing the capacity to consent due to their health condition.
Legislation also sets criteria for 'advance requests' for medically assisted death
· CBC News
· Posted: Oct 27, 2026 10:54 AM EDT | Last Updated: 32 minutes ago
The federal government has tabled new legislation that excludes people suffering solely from mental illness from qualifying for medically assisted death.
Justice Minister Sean Fraser had said earlier this month that Ottawa decided not to move forward with plans to expand MAID access "in circumstances where mental illness is the sole basis."
"While there is not a perfect consensus on this issue, we believe this is the correct approach at this particular time," he said on Oct. 7.

items: Ottawa to indefinitely extend MAID exclusion for people solely suffering from mental illness

blocks.text: The legislation tabled on Tuesday would amend the Criminal Code to "clarify that a person cannot receive medical assistance in dying on the basis of a mental illness."
It also would allow people to make what's known as an "advance request" for medically assisted death before losing the capacity to consent due to their health condition.

But the legislation outlines specific criteria that must be met, including being in "an advanced state of irreversible decline in capability" and "experiencing enduring and intolerable physical or psychological suffering that cannot be relieved through reasonable means."
Fraser and federal Health Minister Marjorie Michel will hold a news conference on Tuesday afternoon to discuss the legislation.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Jillian Kestler-D'Amours is a senior writer at CBC based in Montreal. You can reach her at jillian.kestler-d.amours@cbc.ca.
